close_reason:
Closing as deferred per bead author's own conclusion. The bead body says: (a) 'this is a latent spec-grammar quibble more than a real bug', (b) 'mail-parser does not produce empty MessageIds vectors from non-empty headers' so the divergence between 'parse failure' and 'empty list' never surfaces in practice, (c) 'The fix would be to thread the parser's distinguish-empty-vs-failure information through mime_tree::HeaderValueTyped' — a mime-tree-side change outside this workspace, (d) 'this bead just notes the dependency'.

The right shape is a mime-tree feature request: change HeaderValueTyped::MessageIds(Vec<String>) and ::URLs(Vec<String>) to carry Option<Vec<String>> so a None can signal parse failure distinctly from a Some(vec![]) parsed-but-empty. Filing that upstream is the path forward; until then, the apply_header_form behaviour preserves the latent quibble. No autonomous action available here. Cycling this through /do-beads would not produce a different outcome.

If mime-tree's API ever changes to expose the distinction, the email.rs:339-365 update is mechanical and can be done as a follow-up bead under that mime-tree-version-bump epic.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:339-365 (apply_header_form for AsMessageIds and AsURLs) returns Value::Null on both:

- Parse failure (mime_tree returned a different HeaderValueTyped variant).
- Successful parse with zero entries (mime_tree::HeaderValueTyped::MessageIds(Vec::new()) and URLs(Vec::new())).

The 'if !ids.is_empty()' / 'if !urls.is_empty()' guard collapses these two cases. Per RFC 8621 §4.1.2.5: 'If parsing fails, the value is null.' The spec language is 'on parse failure' not 'on empty list'. A well-formed In-Reply-To header with zero msg-ids (legal per RFC 5322 §3.6.4, which lets In-Reply-To and References be 1*msg-id but a parser that returned the empty list rather than rejecting could conceivably emit []) would be silently converted to null.

In practice this is unlikely to cause user-observable bugs because:

- mail-parser does not produce empty MessageIds vectors from non-empty headers (verified by reading mail-parser source). Either it finds at least one msg-id and returns it, or it returns no MessageIds variant at all.
- Real-world In-Reply-To headers are always 1+ msg-id; clients tolerate null/[] interchangeably.

So this is a latent spec-grammar quibble more than a real bug. Track it for the eventual mime-tree behavioural-contract documentation work. If mime-tree ever changes its parser to produce empty vectors as a 'parsed but no msg-ids found' signal, the bug becomes visible.

The fix would be to thread the parser's distinguish-empty-vs-failure information through mime_tree::HeaderValueTyped — e.g. wrap the Vec in Option (None = parse failure, Some(vec) = parsed, possibly empty). That's a mime-tree-side change; this bead just notes the dependency.
title: AsMessageIds/AsURLs cannot distinguish parse failure from empty list
